Today I had an errand to run in a neighboring town 20-something miles away. I had to travel on a county highway. It's scenic farmland, so there are all kinds of cattle to see along the way, as well as a few places with alpacas/llamas, goats, and horses.

I've mentioned in a different post that we don't have a whole lot of traffic in the area. Don't let that mislead you, we do have traffic slow-downs occasionally.

In the course of my journey today, I had to stop and wait as Ms./Mr. Skunk moseyed across the road. S/he looked for all the world as though s/he was trying to decide whether or not the grass really did look greener on the other side.

About a mile down the road, a calf was out of the field and sauntering down the highway. It wasn't in any particular hurry and didn't seem to have a care in the world. Good neighbor protocol in such situations is stopping at the nearest house and telling that a calf is out down the road. I was in something of a hurry, so I called a friend who lives in the area and asked him to call the two or three farms that the calf might have belonged to.

Another mile or so down the road from the calf, I saw a coyote running across a field. Most farmers don't like coyotes, and with good reason, but I love to see them! So although he didn't actually slow me down by being in the road, I did slow down to watch him.

On the return trip, I had to slow down for a young doe to cross the road in front of me. Deers are beautiful and amazingly graceful animals, so it's always very cool to see them.

So, yeah, out here in the sticks we might not have much traffic, but we do have some rather pleasant slow-downs.
